title: Architecture: replace agent-held BRC waits with deterministic event-pump + durable per-agent memory
v2_change_log: v2 replaces every `claude -p` reference with the correct primitive: `python3 -m egg_agent` invoked via `egg_agent.build_agent_command()`. The `claude --print` form is the EGG100-linted anti-pattern per docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md:90-104 (exits after one response, cannot use tools, cannot handle multi-turn work). The correct primitive is the SDK entry point that is ALREADY in production in the very file this issue rewrites (orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py:748-759 — comment 'Uses the Agent SDK entry point instead of the claude CLI'). The refine analysis at .egg-state/drafts/2908-analysis.md:41-58 explicitly corrected this; v1 inherited the issue body's incorrect phrasing instead of the refine analysis's correction. Both reviewers flagged this as blocking.

v2 spells out the cq-3 durability fix (risk_analyst blocking issue #2). The existing contract_store + state_store primitive is NOT durable enough: orchestrator/state_store.py:11 / :804-805 / :890-928 use 'Best-effort async push to remote after every commit'; orchestrator/contract_store.py:139-142 docstring confirms 'pre-push crashes' lose the local commit. v1's claim that 'branch-committed via the existing schemaVersion 1.2 migrator pattern' satisfies cq-3 was factually wrong about the durability properties. v2 slice-2 specifies (a) a new `_save_pipeline_durable` / `commit_and_push_sync` variant that returns ONLY after `git push origin <branch>` completes, used for HITL-resolution + safety-budget transitions; (b) the schema additions stay; (c) a new `_startup_reconciliation_replay_safety_budget` step that primes the in-memory health_monitor.py:82-103 anchors from durable storage on every host boot.

v2 subdivides v1's slice-2 (reviewer_plan blocking issue #3) into THREE slices along the orchestrator-route / sandbox-CLI / contract-schema seams, with the cq-3 schema first to feed the wrapper consumer: slice-2 (durable persistence schema + sync-flush + startup_reconciliation), slice-3 (next-action HTTP endpoint), slice-4 (net-new CLI verbs). Each is one-reviewer-surface; lifecycle decoding requirements (#2749 dual-role producer-first, #2142 open-NACK barrier, conditional ACK, #2482 stale-version re-review, resolve_obligation) are concentrated in slice-3 with explicit unit-test acceptance criteria.

v2 commits slice-5 (was slice-3) to distilled / rewrite-and-distill memory shape as the DEFAULT (reviewer_plan blocking issue #4), with rationale on BOTH axes: cache cost (distilled rewrites burst the per-event prefix but the burst is bounded by a section template) AND orient-don't-constrain per docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md (distilled summaries orient without flooding the per-event agent's attention; unbounded append-only eventually constrains attention as sea-of-context). The refine analysis at lines 360-367 makes this decision rule explicit; v1's punt-to-slice-3-against-slice-1-data left the choice deferred. Slice-1 spike measurement is reframed as a CHECK on whether the distilled burst materially busts cache on Qwen, not the gating decision.

v2 addresses risk_analyst's flag (prior-fix preservation across BRC preamble collapse, beyond the architect's own R7) by adding an explicit prior-fix-preservation-audit acceptance criterion to slice-7, enumerating #2323 / #2064 / #2482 / #1995 / #2036 / #2451 / #2142 / #2725 and classifying each as (a) orchestrator-side enforced, (b) CLI-level enforced, or (c) prompt-instruction-only.

v2 addresses non-blocking review notes inline: dropped the 'parallel to slice-1' sentence in slice-1's narrative (the YAML's dependencies field IS a hard chain — clarified that the chain is structural, not empirical-data-gated); tightened the patterns.py allowlist citation to span all roles (`patterns.py:362-516+` covers ARCHITECT / TASK_PLANNER / RISK_ANALYST / APPLIER / REVIEWER_* / REFINER) and added matchers.py:33 evidence that `<prefix>/` matches subdirs (prefix-glob semantics, so `<role>/` subdir under `.egg-state/agent-outputs/` is allowed without allowlist changes); explicitly states slice-5 handler memory writes use the dict-arg handler interface (NOT argv — preserves the #2741 mitigation); slice-6 explicitly states the wrapper invokes the existing `egg-orch message wait-loop` CLI rather than rolling its own wait/cursor logic (preserves the #2323 fix); slice-6 includes a cutover playbook (drain in-flight pipelines before deploy); slice-7 adds R5 mitigation contract clarity.

Slice DAG grows from 6 slices to 8 slices but remains a forest (linear chain 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 with slices 7 and 8 as siblings under 6). Slice numbering shifts: v1 slice-3 becomes v2 slice-5; v1 slice-4 becomes v2 slice-6; v1 slice-5 becomes v2 slice-7; v1 slice-6 becomes v2 slice-8.
summary: Reframe a consensus agent from a persistent participant that holds a wait_loop into a stateless per-event handler the wrapper invokes. The deterministic outer loop is the wrapper (`bash -c` heredoc in orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py:116-713), blocking on the existing `egg-orch message wait-loop` CLI; on each actionable event it invokes `python3 -m egg_agent` (via the Agent SDK entry point `egg_agent.build_agent_command()` ALREADY in production at consensus_wrapper.py:748-759 — NOT the EGG100-linted `claude --print` form per docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md:90-104, which exits after one response and cannot use tools or handle multi-turn work) with the agent's cached prefix + a durable distilled memory file (.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md, default DISTILLED shape per the refine analysis at lines 360-367) + the one event payload. The agent acts (review/ACK/NACK/propose/confirm), updates its memory via the dict-arg handler interface (NOT argv — preserves the #2741 shell-metachar mitigation), and exits naturally — exit code 0 is success, not a restart trigger. The wrapper loops until the orchestrator reports the role consensus-confirmed and is_complete. This removes the model-driven re-entry seam at the root of the qwen3.7-max fall-out (#2906) — the entire BRC-wait bug lineage (#2323, #2064/#2482, #2036, #1995, #2451) becomes inapplicable because the model no longer drives the wait. The agent primitive (pod, worktree, role, SDK, gateway-enforced file-write boundary, EGG_AGENT_ROLE) is untouched. The change is deletion-heavy inside the consensus subsystem: the 3-restart FAIL cap (consensus_wrapper.py:38), the `_RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` + `_RECOVERY_USER_PROMPT` recovery machinery (consensus_wrapper.py:64-105), the SSE consensus.reached blocking path in the wrapper (consensus_wrapper.py:397-548), and the agent's `_start_wait_loop_heartbeat` ticker (sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py:234-264) all go away. cq-3's HARD requirement for durable HITL + safety-budget state surviving SDLC-host failure is met by a NEW synchronous-flush variant of save_pipeline (`commit_and_push_sync`) used specifically for those rare mutations + a new `_startup_reconciliation_replay_safety_budget` step on host boot — the existing best-effort-async-push primitive (state_store.py:11/:804-805/:890-928) does NOT meet cq-3 on its own. Per operator decisions: cq-1 splits the 28-MCP-tool collapse to a follow-up issue but requires this issue ship any net-new CLI verbs the new wrapper invokes; cq-2 ships Qwen on the new event-pump directly (no legacy fallback); cq-3 makes durable server-side persistence of the no-progress safety budget + parked HITL decision a HARD requirement; cq-4 deletes the old capped-restart wrapper path entirely with no flagged fallback.

recommended_approach.name: Stateless event-pump wrapper + durable per-role memory (distilled default) + server-side next-action endpoint; `python3 -m egg_agent` per event via `build_agent_command()`; cq-3 durable persistence via sync-flush + startup_reconciliation; legacy capped-restart wrapper deleted in-issue
recommended_approach.summary: The wrapper is the deterministic outer loop; the agent is a per-event handler. Five server-side primitives carry continuity: (1) cq-3 durable persistence schema + sync-flush helper + startup_reconciliation; (2) `consensus next-action` endpoint; (3) net-new CLI verbs (`brc list-blocking`, `phase get-context`, `brc next-action`) — all using `_handler_dispatch` for parity with MCP; (4) per-agent distilled memory (.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md) written via the dict-arg handler interface on each brc_ack/brc_nack; (5) the event-pump wrapper itself. The 28 agent-facing MCP tools are NOT collapsed in this issue (cq-1 follow-up).
why_recommended: Removes the model-driven re-entry seam that this entire bug lineage depends on (the issue's root cause): `message_wait_loop` (sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py:267, line :405-410 first-match return) returns on a single event, requiring the model to volunteer to re-enter the wait. Claude usually re-enters; qwen3.7-max does not (#2906) and exits success=True at ~30-50 of a 1000-turn budget. A deterministic outer loop in bash + the existing `egg-orch message wait-loop` CLI cannot fall out of the wait regardless of model.

Net-removes custom code: the BRC mechanism converges to the existing SDK entry point (`python3 -m egg_agent` via `build_agent_command()`) that the wrapper template ALREADY uses today at consensus_wrapper.py:748-759. The bash wrapper shrinks dramatically (the 700-line `_CONSENSUS_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE` is mostly recovery + restart machinery being deleted). The 28 agent-facing MCP tools and 8 namespace files are untouched in THIS issue (cq-1 follow-up) but the action surface for the event-pump is the existing `egg-orch` / `egg-contract` CLIs, which already share handler functions with the MCP tools (sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:2528-2805 + the shared dispatch pattern verified by tests/tools/test_mcp_cli_drift.py).

Inherits gateway-enforced file-write boundaries unchanged: each per-event `python3 -m egg_agent` invocation runs in the same pod with the same EGG_AGENT_ROLE env var → tool_interceptor.check_file_write_permission (shared/egg_agent/tool_interceptor.py:27) on the sandbox side, validate_agent_push on the gateway side (gateway/agent_restrictions.py, imported at gateway/phase_filter.py:1081-1083). `.egg-state/agent-outputs/` is in every BRC-participating role's allowlist (shared/egg_restrictions/patterns.py:362-516+ covers ARCHITECT, TASK_PLANNER, RISK_ANALYST, APPLIER, REVIEWER_*, REFINER); matchers.py:33 confirms `<prefix>/` is prefix-glob and matches subdirs, so `<role>/brc-memory.md` requires no allowlist change.

Satisfies cq-3's durable persistence HARD requirement via a NEW `commit_and_push_sync` variant of save_pipeline used for the rare HITL-resolution + safety-budget transition writes — the existing best-effort-async-push primitive (state_store.py:11 / :804-805 / :890-928) does NOT meet cq-3 on its own (contract_store.py:139-142 docstring confirms 'pre-push crashes' lose the local commit). Combined with a NEW `_startup_reconciliation_replay_safety_budget` step on every host boot that primes the in-memory health_monitor.py:82-103 anchors from durable storage, the test for host-recoverability ('inject host-kill mid-budget, fresh host resumes from persisted state') passes against the new primitive.

Per-route caching is a measured non-issue for both routes under the new control flow at the short/medium timescales (#2908 comments): the Anthropic route has a 1h TTL with the dynamic <env> sitting in the uncached suffix (no commit/cwd/date bust of the ~17K stable prefix); the Qwen route has cross-session caching (~99.99%) that survives ≥5.5min idle measured. The only remaining unknown is the Qwen TTL ceiling around 15 min worst-case BRC idle — slice-1 measures it, slice-8 conditionally adds bounded keep-warm only if that gap exists.

rejected_options_summary.B_prompt_only_mitigation_for_qwen: Tighten the BRC preamble's stay-alive language to nudge qwen3.7-max into re-entering wait_loop. Rejected because it narrows the seam for one model rather than removing it; the issue body explicitly calls this out ("prompt-only mitigations only narrow the seam for one model; they don't remove it"). Past stack-loop guard bugs (#2036, #1995, #2451, #2323, #2064, #2482) all stem from the agent-held wait assumption and would recur on the next prompt-fragile model.
rejected_options_summary.C_custom_streaming_harness_with_resume: Build a persistent streaming session with SDK `--resume` so the agent never tears down between events. Rejected because (a) it adds a third execution structure to egg (alongside one-shot agents and the BRC consensus subsystem) — exactly the custom-harness path the issue body explicitly excludes ("no custom harness; drops the persistent-streaming-session idea entirely"); (b) the `--resume` thread retains the model-driven re-entry property that this issue is trying to delete.
rejected_options_summary.D_keep_legacy_wrapper_behind_flag: Ship the new event-pump path beside the old capped-restart wrapper, keep the old path as a flagged opt-out. Rejected by cq-4: operator explicitly directed "delete the old capped-restart wrapper path entirely — do NOT retain it behind a flag". The no-progress safety budget from cq-3 becomes the SOLE safety net under the new design.

slices.name: WS0 de-risking spike — event-pump prototype + Qwen cache TTL measurement
slices.summary: Build a minimal throwaway wrapper that loops `python3 -m egg_agent` (via `build_agent_command()` — NOT `claude -p`) per BRC event against the existing `egg-orch message wait-loop` CLI + existing MCP tool surface, run it on the #2906 reproducer (issue-2270, qwen3.7-max), and measure Qwen-route provider-cache survival across the full worst-case BRC idle (~15 min target — observed BRC idles reached 10-13 min for a producer composing a response to a NACK). Output: a `docs/spike/` report (architect / doc-updater write-scoped) covering (a) consensus reached without the 3-restart churn; (b) Qwen-route TTL measured from the litellm / `cost_callback` state files (`~/.local/state/clm/cost-*.json`), since Claude Code's `usage.*` returns all-zero on the Qwen route; (c) per-event cold-read cost across consecutive per-event invocations and across the injected long idle. Anthropic-route TTL is already cleared in the WS7 empirical comment. Slice-1 informs slice-5 (memory shape: a CHECK on the architect's committed distilled default, NOT a gating decision) and slice-8 (cache decision tree). Downstream slices 2-7 do NOT structurally depend on slice-1's empirical numbers; the linear chain is structural (each slice consumes the previous deliverable), not data-gated.
slices.evidence: consensus_wrapper.py:116-713 (existing template to prototype against); consensus_wrapper.py:748-759 (`build_agent_command()` is the existing SDK entry point — NOT `claude -p`); sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py:267 (`message_wait_loop` provides the long-block primitive needed by the prototype); #2906 reproducer is issue-2270 on qwen3.7-max.

slices.name: cq-3 durable HITL + no-progress-budget persistence schema (sync-flush + startup_reconciliation)
slices.summary: Land the durable server-side persistence schema that replaces the in-memory + best-effort-async-push primitive. Three additions: (a) new `_save_pipeline_durable(state)` / `commit_and_push_sync(state)` variant of save_pipeline that returns ONLY after `git push origin <branch>` completes successfully — used for HITL-resolution writes AND safety-budget transition writes; other contract writes keep the existing best-effort-async path so high-frequency writes are not regressed; (b) new contract fields `pipeline.no_progress_budget` (durable counter + threshold + state) and `pipeline.parked_hitl` (the currently-parked decision + its resume token), landed via the existing schemaVersion 1.2 migrator pattern, defaults preserve current behavior (None/0); (c) new `_startup_reconciliation_replay_safety_budget` step on orchestrator boot that re-reads the durable `pipeline.no_progress_budget` from the on-branch contract for every active pipeline and primes the in-memory health_monitor.py:82-103 anchors (currently initialised-to-zero on every restart). No consumers wired yet — schema and sync-flush helper land here; slice-6 consumes both. Hard constraint: the host-recoverability test (inject host-kill mid-budget, fresh host resumes from persisted state) MUST pass against the new primitive — failing here means the sole safety net under cq-4 is broken before it ships.
slices.evidence: orchestrator/state_store.py:11 ('async push via a daemon thread'), :804-805 ('Best-effort async push to remote after every commit' → `self._sync_to_remote_async()`), :890-928 (debounced daemon-thread push), :127 (`_push_in_flight: ClassVar[bool]`); orchestrator/contract_store.py:139-142 (load_contract_from_branch docstring confirms 'pre-push crashes' failure mode); orchestrator/health_monitor.py:82-103 (in-memory anchors initialised-to-zero on restart); existing schemaVersion 1.2 migrator pattern (in production from #2777 slice-1b).

slices.name: Server-side next-action endpoint (orchestrator/routes — pure additive)
slices.summary: Land the `consensus next-action --role R` HTTP endpoint (or extension of `consensus status --json` per od-3) on the orchestrator that returns the next action the role should take. Judgment stays with the agent; the endpoint owns sequencing only. Lifecycle decoding requirements (must be covered by endpoint return values + unit tests): dual-role producer-first ordering (#2749), open-NACK barrier (#2142), conditional ACK paths, stale-version re-review (#2482), resolve_obligation surface. The endpoint MAY surface the slice-2 durable `no_progress_budget` state in its response so the wrapper's safety-budget consumer (slice-6) reads it via a single endpoint call. If extending `consensus status --json` is sufficient (verified against the lifecycle requirements), prefer that — od-3 defers to verification. Pure additive route work; no consumer changes; backwards-compatible.
slices.evidence: sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:2783 (existing `consensus status` verb shared with `mcp__brc__get_state` per orch_cli.py:2785-2805 — the extension target); existing route registration patterns in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py; #2142 open-NACK aggregation barrier; #2482 stale-version re-review; #2749 dual-role producer-first ordering.

slices.name: Net-new CLI verbs (sandbox/egg_lib only — `brc list-blocking`, `phase get-context`, `brc next-action`)
slices.summary: Wrap the slice-3 next-action endpoint and the existing `mcp__brc__list_blocking` / `mcp__phase__get_context` handlers with CLI verbs that satisfy the cq-1 net-new-CLI requirement (build any net-new CLI verbs the new wait-loop / event-pump depends on; do NOT delete existing MCP tools — that collapse is the cq-1 follow-up). slices.name: `brc-memory.md` artifact (distilled default) + brc_ack/brc_nack handler memory-write scaffolding (dict-arg path)
slices.summary: Define the durable per-role memory file that carries continuity between per-event `python3 -m egg_agent` invocations, and wire its writes into the handler layer that already runs on every ACK/NACK. The file format is markdown with structured sections (codebase/change model, per-producer assessment, decision log) anchored by stable headings so the agent can read-modify-write deterministically. Written to `.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md`. brc_ack and brc_nack already receive `reason` + `files_reviewed` via the dict-arg handler interface (sandbox-side in-process MCP, NOT argv — preserves the #2741 mitigation); the handler appends a structured entry to the memory file on each ACK/NACK. Retention per refine Q2: ephemeral coordination state cleaned up with the pod; orchestrator message history is the durable reconstruction backstop. Hard caveat from refine Q2 stands: if implement-time evidence shows the memory file is load-bearing for correct recovery after host/pod restart, this slice is revisited. **Memory shape is COMMITTED to distilled / rewrite-and-distill (NOT punted to a decision rule)** per the refine analysis at lines 360-367. Rationale on BOTH axes: (axis-1 cache cost) distilled rewrites burst the per-event prefix on each ACK/NACK but the burst is bounded by a section template so size + frequency are predictable; slice-1's spike is a CHECK on whether the burst materially busts Qwen prefix cache; (axis-2 orient-don't-constrain per docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md) distilled summaries orient without flooding the per-event agent's attention; unbounded append-only eventually constrains as sea-of-context. If slice-1's WS0 measurement shows distilled bursts materially bust cache on Qwen, slice-5 MAY add a bounded append-only tail with explicit compaction — but the default is distilled and the decision is made now.

slices.name: Event-pump consensus_wrapper + wrapper-side liveness migration + safety-budget consumer + legacy deletion
slices.summary: The central control-flow rewrite. The wrapper becomes a deterministic event pump: blocks on the existing `egg-orch message wait-loop` CLI (wrapper invokes the CLI directly; does NOT roll its own wait/cursor logic — preserves the #2323 cursor-threading fix at /tmp/egg-wait-cursor-*), invokes `python3 -m egg_agent` via `build_agent_command()` (NOT `claude -p` — EGG100 anti-pattern) per actionable event, and loops until the orchestrator reports the role consensus-confirmed and is_complete. Four tightly-coupled pieces: (a) WS1 — rewrite `_CONSENSUS_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE` (consensus_wrapper.py:116-713); clean agent exit after handling one event is expected, not a restart trigger; delete `MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS = 3` (line 38), restart loop (lines 555-695), `_RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (lines 64-99), `_RECOVERY_USER_PROMPT` (lines 102-105), and the SSE consensus.reached blocking path (lines 397-548 including curl SSE consumer at :419-501) — cq-4 mandates no flagged fallback; (b) WS4 — move heartbeat + gateway-session keep-alive ownership from `_start_wait_loop_heartbeat` ticker (sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py:175 + :234-264 at `_WAIT_LOOP_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECS = 60s` at message.py:47) to the wrapper's wait; wrapper invokes the existing `egg-orch message heartbeat` CLI verb (orch_cli.py:1832) at the same 60s cadence; orchestrator-side threshold consumer (orchestrator/health_monitor.py:771, 120s default / 600s implement) unchanged; (c) safety-budget consumer wired against the slice-2 durable `pipeline.no_progress_budget` field — when exhausted, fire OVERSEER_ALERT + open HITL (resume/abort) using slice-2 durable parked-HITL state; on host death + restart, wrapper re-reads via slice-2's `_startup_reconciliation_replay_safety_budget` and resumes monitoring the same budget (cq-3 HARD requirement); (d) the SSE blocking path collapses to a single `egg-orch consensus check` against the slice-3 endpoint — orchestrator/sse.py:111 (SSEClientManager) STAYS for the operator-facing stream (out of scope per cq-1). orchestrator/concurrent_executor.py:37 import of `build_consensus_wrapped_command` is rewired to the new template. Minimal agent-prompt change: drop the stay-alive loop instruction from `_build_brc_preamble` (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:12348) so the agent exits after handling one event — FULL preamble collapse stays in slice-7. **Cutover playbook:** drain in-flight pipelines on the old wrapper before deploying this slice's PR; new pipelines start on the event-pump at deploy time; no flagged fallback per cq-4. This slice has the largest blast radius; the BRC cycle MAY need in-slice subdivision (6a wrapper-side heartbeat CLI verb additive; 6b wrapper template rewrite + rewire + deletion sweep) if the producer hits >3 NACK rounds — flagged but not pre-subdivided because cq-4 forbids retaining the old path through any intermediate state.

slices.name: Prompt collapse + delta-scoped re-analysis + prior-fix preservation audit
slices.summary: Retire the agent-side mechanics the agent no longer owns. Two coupled pieces: (a) WS6 prompt collapse — replace STAY-ALIVE / wait-loop / cursor-threading / pre-confirm-wait foot-gun text in `_build_brc_preamble` (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:12348, call sites :13659, :13692, :13720) and in sandbox/agent-config/rules/*.md with a lean event-handler contract; **prior-fix preservation audit (risk_analyst flag):** the preamble currently embeds prompt-instruction versions of #2323 cursor-threading, #2064/#2482 pre-confirm-wait, #1995 gap-race, #2036 reviewer heartbeats, #2451 gateway keep-alive, #2142 open-NACK aggregation, #2725 producer-allowlist scope — the collapse MUST enumerate each fix and classify it as (a) orchestrator-side enforced (safe to remove from prompt), (b) CLI-level enforced (safe — wrapper uses CLI), or (c) prompt-instruction-only (REQUIRES preservation in the lean handler contract); the task acceptance criterion gates the audit. open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.topic: Memory file shape (append-only vs rewrite-and-distill) — RESOLVED at architect tier in v2
open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.resolution: COMMITTED to distilled / rewrite-and-distill as the DEFAULT per the refine analysis lines 360-367. Rationale on both axes: cache cost (bounded burst by section template) AND orient-don't-constrain (distilled summaries orient without flooding attention). Slice-1 spike is a CHECK on Qwen cache behavior, not the gating decision. Slice-5 MAY add a bounded append-only tail with explicit compaction if measurement shows distilled busts Qwen cache materially.

open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.topic: SDK `--resume` for NACK→re-review thread only vs uniform fresh+memory everywhere
open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.decision_rule: Default to uniform fresh+memory; reconsider `--resume` for the tightly-coupled NACK→re-review thread only if measurement shows the memory-only path loses material continuity.

open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.topic: Next-action surface — reuse `consensus status` vs new `consensus next-action` endpoint
open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.decision_rule: Prefer extending `consensus status --json` if the current payload is close to sufficient (verify against producer/reviewer/dual-role + open-NACK barrier #2142 + conditional ACK + stale-version re-review #2482 + resolve_obligation). Only add a new verb if extension would mix concerns.

open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.topic: Idle/no-progress safety budget shape (wall-clock vs no-event vs hybrid)
open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.decision_rule: Schema is durable per cq-3. Shape options: (a) wall-clock budget per phase; (b) no-event-budget (no actionable event for N seconds); (c) hybrid. Slice-2 chooses; slice-6 wires.
Three-outcome decision tree based on slice-1 TTL ceiling measurement.

open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.topic: WS8 latency trade — CLI subprocess overhead per per-event invocation
open_decisions_to_resolve_during_impleme.decision_rule: Spike measures per-event wall-clock with CLI invocations. If subprocess + interpreter spawn cost is non-trivial, fallback is a persistent `egg-orch` daemon/socket or batched calls. Default: a handful of CLI calls per event is negligible.
